body: Implement ADR-0015 (docs/adr/0015-segmented-gate-manifest.md) and the normative spec (docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md) authored by T-MANIFEST-FOREST-SPEC. Problem being solved: .adlc/manifest.jsonl is a single hash-chained committed ledger — every entry carries seq (strictly increasing), prev = sha256 of the previous raw line's exact bytes, and an HMAC-SHA256 sig (sigVersion 2 signs ALL fields including seq and prev, key env ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY; see packages/gate-manifest/lib/sign.mjs). Every gate appends through appendManifestEntry (packages/gate-manifest/lib/record.mjs), so any two concurrent branches collide at the tail: a guaranteed textual merge conflict whose resolution requires rewriting seq/prev, which invalidates v2 signatures and therefore requires the signing key. The fix: freeze the root file and append new evidence to per-lineage segment files, so concurrent branches write different files and no merge ever rewrites a chained line. Implementation slices, in release order (readers MUST ship before any writer produces segments): (1) Forest read layer — verify/show/attest in packages/gate-manifest and the manifest readEntries consumers walk the root .adlc/manifest.jsonl PLUS .adlc/manifest.d/*.jsonl segments; each segment is an internal hash chain whose first entry carries a fork anchor {segment, seq, hash-of-last-raw-line} binding it into committed history; a segments-free repo must verify and read byte-for-byte identically to today (golden regression tests). (2) Cross-model reader — packages/prosecute/lib/cross-model.mjs walks the forest and applies the cross-segment revocation semantics decided in ADR-0015. (3) Writer — appendManifestEntry routes to the current lineage's segment once the repo carries the cutover marker; per-segment ledger lock via withLedgerLock; signing unchanged (v2, per-entry). (4) Greenfield scaffold — packages/init scaffolds new repos directly on the segmented layout so they never need migration. (5) Migration ceremony — `adlc gate-manifest migrate`: dry-run by default, --write to apply; verifies every existing signature under ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY before touching anything; freezes the root WITHOUT rewriting its bytes (existing sigs stay valid); writes a hash-named backup; records a cutover evidence entry; seals every standing root approve with a signed needs-attention entry immediately before cutover (ADR-0015/spec §4.6) rather than refusing to migrate — this is a deliberate reset forcing fresh re-approval, not an oversight. (6) CI gates — generalize rails-guard's append-only check (packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/manifest.mjs assertAppendOnly) to per-segment byte-prefix (every segment file present at base must be a byte-prefix of itself at HEAD; new segment files must anchor to a line that exists in committed history) and extend validateMigrationEvidence for the cutover entry. (7) repair-chain becomes per-segment. (8) Docs (docs/tools/gate-manifest.md) and a doctor check for orphaned/dangling anchors. Constraints: do NOT migrate this repository's manifest in the implementation diff (that is T-MANIFEST-FOREST-MIGRATE); preserve all existing guarantees — tamper evidence, HMAC provenance, append-only-in-PRs, provider revocation ordering (#326), migration-evidence validation, and the documented truncation limit (no better, no worse). This work is trust-root tier (packages/gate-manifest, packages/prosecute, packages/rails-guard): P5 prosecution requires a distinct-provider cross-model-review approve bound to the reviewed revision before merge. Acceptance criteria and verification methods: (a) full repo test suite passes — `npm test`; (b) golden tests prove a segments-free repo reads/verifies identically before and after — run the new regression suite; (c) adversarial tamper tests cover: garbled segment line, dangling fork anchor, anchor to a nonexistent line, duplicate segment filename, stale anchor presenting alternative history, unsigned entry in a keyed verify — each must fail closed with a named reason (node --test on the new test files); (d) per-segment append-only enforcement has a test that rewrites a committed segment byte and observes deny — run it; (e) `adlc hollow-test` and `adlc behavior-diff` run clean on the change; (f) P5 prosecution passes including the gated cross-model approve — `adlc prosecute --base main` exits 0.
title: Implement the segmented gate-manifest (chain forest) with migration ceremony
